texts.preamble: T. Shafiulla, vs The State Of Ap Rep By Its Pp Hyd., on 13 April, 2022 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Tarlada Rajasekhar Rao Crl.R.C.No.295 of 2013 Order:
texts.facts: - The Food Inspector, Division-I, Kadapa District filed the complaint against the accused under Section.7(V) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short, "the Act") r/w Rules.49(28) and 50(1) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (for short, "the Rules") punishable under Section.16(1)(a)(ii) of the Act. 2. On 09.01.2010 at about 12:30 P.M. LW.1, G.Sreesailam, Food Inspector along with his office subordinate Sri Seetharamaiah and Tahsildar of Chennur by name Smt B. Santhamma visited M/s. Thulasi Packaged Drinking water i.e., the premises of the petitioner/accused herein and found that the accused was present and he was transacting business and manufacturing Thulasi Packaged Drinking Water for sale for human consumption. LW1 Food Inspector disclosed his identity and the purpose of inspection and called one mediator namely S. Md.Waris. In the presence of the mediator, the Food Inspector inspected the said water unit and found that they were manufacturing 200 ml sealed water packets and filling 20 litres cans of Thulasi Packaged Drinking Water. On enquiry, about the purpose for which they were manufacturing the water packets and filling the cans, it is stated that it is for the sale to the public for human consumption. 3. Then the Food Inspector also enquired the accused with regard to obtaining the B.I.S. certificate and P.F.A. License. The accused stated that he is having no objection certificate from the Gram Panchayat, Chennur Village and they are not having any B.I.S. certificate and P.F.A. license. Then the Food Inspector drafted panchanama as per procedure and filed the charge sheet. 4. Basing on the charge sheet, the Court of learned I Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Kadapa conducted the trial and convicted the accused vide judgment dated 14.06.2011. 5. The contention of the petitioner is that he has not obtained B.I.S. certificate and P.F.A. license. The evidence of PW1 coupled with Ex P5 shows that, when PW1 went along with Tahsildar, Chennur, he observed the accused manufacturing packaged drinking water in sealed packets and 20 litres cans. 6. Heard both sides. 10. Aggrieved by the said judgment, the petitioner filed Criminal Appeal No.91 of 2011 on the file of the Court of the learned VI Additional Sessions Judge, Kadapa.
texts.arguments: 7. The learned trial Court, relying on the judgment in "Krishna Foods & Acqua Minerals, Nallajerla and others Vs. Government of India, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Department of Health) T. Shafiulla, vs The State Of Ap Rep By Its Pp Hyd., on 13 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10218592/ 1 and another," reported in 2004 (6) ALT 4 (D.B.), which stated that, for the manufacture, sale or exhibition for sale of packaged drinking water, a certification mark from the Bureau of Indian Standards is mandatory. 8. 11. Aggrieved by the same, the present Criminal Revision Case is filed before this Court stating that there is no evidence of proof that the packed water was sold in the market and that any complaint by consumer against the manufacturer is given. He contended that without there being any complaint given by the consumer, the said complaint is not maintainable against the manufacturing unit. 12. Learned counsel for the petitioner has not raised any valid grounds muchless the question of law was not involved in the afore mentioned grounds.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 11. Aggrieved by the same, the present Criminal Revision Case is filed before this Court stating that there is no evidence of proof that the packed water was sold in the market and that any complaint by consumer against the manufacturer is given. He contended that without there being any complaint given by the consumer, the said complaint is not maintainable against the manufacturing unit. 12. Learned counsel for the petitioner has not raised any valid grounds muchless the question of law was not involved in the afore mentioned grounds.
